- nda-19: Survival of obligations | Some obligations of Agreement may survive termination of Agreement.
- nda-8: Notice on compelled disclosure | Receiving Party shall notify Disclosing Party in case Receiving Party is required by law, regulation or judicial process to disclose any Confidential Information.

Thought: Let me analyze each hypothesis against the document segments.

- nda-19 (Survival of obligations): No mention of obligations surviving termination. NotMentioned.
- nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment [11] says Recipient must prevent disclosure even if authorized/directed under law, without express permission of Discloser. This contradicts a duty to notify — actually it addresses compelled disclosure but requires prevention, not notification. The hypothesis says "shall notify" — the document doesn't say notify; it says prevent disclosure even if required by law. This is arguably a Contradiction since instead of notifying and complying, the Recipient must refuse disclosure. Evidence: [11], [12].
- nda-11 (No reverse engineering): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-12 (Permissible development of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-1 (Explicit identification): Segment [7] mentions "Confidential Information as identified and reduced in writing or provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." Since information can be provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing, not all CI must be expressly identified. This contradicts "All Confidential Information shall be expressly identified." Evidence: [7]. Contradiction.
- nda-16 (Return of confidential information): Not mentioned. Segment [14] says layout plan always in custody of Discloser, but no return/destruction upon termination. NotMentioned.
- nda-10 (Confidentiality of Agreement): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-2 (None-inclusion of non-technical information): Segment [3] lists CI including "services, customers etc" — customers is non-technical. So Contradiction. Evidence: [3].
- nda-15 (No licensing): Not explicitly mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-20 (Permissible post-agreement possession): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-18 (No solicitation): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-7 (Sharing with third-parties): Segment [10] says no sharing with any Third Party under any circumstances. Contradiction. Evidence: [10].
- nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar information): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Segment [10] prohibits sharing with any Third Party; employees might not be third parties. Not explicitly addressed. NotMentioned.
- nda-17 (Permissible copy): Not mentioned. NotMentioned.
- nda-4 (Limited use): Segment [10] "No Use: Recipient agrees not to use the Confidential Information in any way" — combined with [5] purpose. Actually [10] says not to use in any way or share. Hmm, the purpose is defined in [5]. The "No Use" clause says not use CI in any way — this supports limited use. Entailment with evidence [10] (and [5]). Actually the hypothesis: "shall not use any CI for any purpose other than the purposes stated." Segment [10] says not to use in any way — that's even stronger, entails limited use. Evidence: [10], possibly [5].
- nda-3 (Inclusion of verbally conveyed information): Segment [7] "provided verbally or in any other way not reduced in writing." Entailment. Evidence: [7].
